title: ResourceOperation
description: An action declared on a single SecureResource (create, read, approve, export, etc.) that the authorization layer can permit or refuse. It carries the access conditions, rate limits and audit settings that apply whenever an actor invokes that action on that resource, and so forms the verb in a subject-verb-object access decision. Use Permission instead when the element is the grant authorizing a role or actor to perform an action, i.e. who may do it, rather than the action as exposed and guarded on the resource. Use SecureResource instead when the element is the protected API, table, file or service itself rather than one of the actions that can be performed on it. Use PolicyAction instead when the element is the enforcement response a policy rule produces (deny, log, redirect, mask), not the operation an actor requests. Use AccessCondition instead when the element is the field-operator-value predicate that must hold before the operation is allowed, rather than the operation it gates.

operation.description: Permitted operation type on the secured resource.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what invoking this operation does to the resource and any business significance (e.g. 'Approves a pending invoice for payment'); set it when the operation verb alone does not make the effect or the sensitivity clear.

conditions.description: References AccessCondition nodes that must be satisfied before this operation is authorized.

rateLimit.description: References RateLimit nodes (api.ratelimit) applied to this operation.

audit.description: References AuditConfig nodes specifying how this operation is logged for accountability.

x-dr-standard: NIST SP 800-53 AC-3 (Access Enforcement); XACML 3.0 Action attribute category
x-dr-evidence: An authorization check naming both a resource type and an action verb, e.g. @PreAuthorize("hasPermission(#id, 'Invoice', 'approve')") or authorize(user, 'export', report).
A per-resource list of actions in an authorization schema or policy file, e.g. an Oso/Cedar/OpenFGA resource block with actions = ["read", "update", "share"].
A controller handler for one verb on one resource wrapped with its own guard, rate-limit and audit-log middleware, e.g. router.post('/orders/:id/approve', requireRole, rateLimit, auditLog, handler).
